title: Procurement & Legal Negotiation Pocket — Private/Hybrid Deals (Draft)
body:
Purpose: quick pocket guide for SEs/AMs when engaging procurement and legal on Private / Hybrid (VPC/on-prem + hosted fallback) deals. Focus: anticipate redlines, prioritize negotiable levers, and preserve product economics while closing enterprise contracts faster.

Status/context: draft; pulled from recent pilots with FinRegCo and HealthOps pilot. Observations: procurement cares about predictability and auditability; legal cares about data boundaries and liability. Both are sensitive to certified controls and visibility into how data and prompts are handled.

Topline messaging (30s):
- We provide a unified inference runtime that can run in your VPC or as dedicated pools with a consistent API, observability, and clear SLAs.
- For regulated customers, we can offer private control-plane + optional on-prem worker nodes, KMS/HSM integrations, and audit logs.
- Commercially: flexible mix of reserved capacity (predictable commit) + usage-based metering for burst. This lets procurement lock unit economics while giving engineering predictable latency.

30–60s buyer-ready lines by role:
- Procurement: "Two levers — commit for steady-state and usage for peaks. We model you to a single blended eCPU/slot price and produce an expected monthly bill with 95th percentile traffic scenarios."
- Legal: "We ship an auditable data flow diagram, integrate with your KMS, and will accept carveouts limited to proven compliance requirements (SOC2/ISO attestation included)."
- CTO/Platform: "Same API surface as hosted. You can pin model versions and rollout with canary policies; we handle KV-caching and prefix caching to keep costs low."

Common procurement asks + recommended responses:
1) "Can we cap monthly spend?"
   - Response: Offer a committed reserved capacity SKU with a floor and an overage rate. Example: 60% of predicted monthly peak purchased as reserved; overage billed at discounted rate. If necessary, add a true hard cap as an optional governance flag but warn of dropped requests and define fallback.

2) "We need predictable unit pricing for budget approvals."
   - Response: Propose a 12-month blended unit cost tied to reserved capacity plus a modeled estimate of burst usage using historic pilot traces. Provide sensitivity table (low/medium/high) and an SLO-based billing appendix.

3) "Can we host everything on-prem?"
   - Response: Yes for worker nodes and inference runtime. Keep control plane options flexible: private control plane over customer network or a hybrid where control plane is hosted but never stores prompt payloads in persistent logs. Offer air-gap package (longer lead, enterprise legal + infra audit).

Top legal friction points + playbook:
- Data residency & processing: Provide explicit data flow diagram and commit to no persistent storage of prompt payloads in hosted logs (or encrypt-at-rest + customer KMS).
- Indemnity & liability caps: We push for mutual indemnity for IP but with standard commercial liability cap (e.g., fee-based cap or tiered carveouts). For regulated verticals, escalate to Legal Ops early; we may accept higher caps with price/milestone tradeoffs.
- Security attestations: Provide SOC2 Type II, ISO summary, and third-party pen test reports. Offer options for additional audits (customer-funded).
- Subprocessors / third parties: Provide current subprocessors list; commit to 30-day notice for changes.

Negotiation levers (ranked):
1) Pricing structure (reserved vs burst) — easiest to trade for concessions and most impact on economics.
2) SLA & financial credits — narrow the SLO or convert credits to service credits tied to availability/latency at route-level.
3) Data residency & KMS control — technical integration work but critical for deal closure; rarely price-sensitive but has implementation lead time.
4) Contractual caps & indemnities — legal teams dig here; escalate for special vertical clauses.

Playbook for SE/AM during procurement/legal cycle:
1) Pre-call prep: attach the short data flow diagram + SOC2 summary + reserved vs hybrid price model (3 scenarios). Link to Confluence template: confluence:INFERENCE-CONTRACT-TEMPLATES-234.
2) Procurement call: lead with economics (blended price + sensitivity table). Record procurement baseline ask (cap/horizon).
3) Legal intro call: confirm required attestations and specific redlines (data residency, liability, audit rights). Ask to track redlines in a shared Google doc.
4) Technical deep dive: map network architecture and required approvals (IP allowlists, peering, HSM certs). SEs: bring infra engineer or solutions engineer.
5) Escalation: if Legal requests non-standard liability or source code escrow, flag to Deals Desk and Legal Ops.

Sample clauses / suggested language (short):
- Data handling: "Provider shall not persist customer prompt/response payloads beyond 14 days in hosted environments; customer may request immediate purge. All persisted data at rest will be encrypted with Customer KMS where configured."
- Subprocessors: "Provider will provide subprocessors list and provide 30 days' notice prior to onboarding a new subprocessor affecting customer data."
- SLA: "Provider commits to 99.5% availability measured monthly for reserved capacity endpoints; service credits apply as outlined in Appendix A."

Concessions we can give (and cost to us):
- Shorter invoice terms (Net 45 -> Net 30): low cost.
- Increased support SLA + named SRE on-call: medium cost; price in as add-on premium.
- Larger indemnity cap: high legal cost; require higher committed revenue or separate insurance certificate.
- On-prem deployment: higher implementation surcharge, longer timeline (8–12 weeks typical).

Deal checklist for close (SE checklist):
- [ ] Confirm reserved capacity baseline and overage rates in writing.
- [ ] Deliver data flow diagram + SOC2 artifacts.
- [ ] Confirm KMS integration plan and timeline.
- [ ] Share sample MSA redlines and capture customer's top 5 contract asks.
- [ ] Align on go-live readiness criteria (canary traffic levels, latency SLOs).

Stall signals & counterplays:
- "We need source code / full access" -> Offer detailed operational runbooks, telemetry and audit logs; source code escrow is expensive; propose escrow for major enterprise deals only and route to Legal Ops.
- "We want unlimited liability" -> Push back with standard cap + customer insurance proof. Tradeoff: higher cap for committed spend or indemnity carveouts for known categories.
- "We need guaranteed model outputs" -> Explain that generative outputs are probabilistic; offer model gating, validation prompt sets and acceptance tests as a contractual appendix.

Handoff template to Legal Ops (copyable snippet):
"Customer: <NAME> | Procurement rep: <NAME> | Primary legal concerns: <list> | Preferred pricing construct: <reserved/burst/hybrid> | Requested liability cap: <value> | Required attestations: <SOC2/ISO/HIPAA> | Notes: <timeline/go-live target>"

Notes to SEs: keep the conversation pragmatic. Focus procurement on dollars and billing predictability, focus legal on attestations and a small set of non-negotiables. Be explicit about lead times for private/hybrid setup (scheduling, network approvals, certs). This doc is a living draft — add fresh redlines and call summaries into the shared doc.
